title: Affine pushforward is perverse up to the relative dimension
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be an
affine morphism of finite
type between separated schemes of finite type over a field $k$,
whose geometric fibers have dimension at most $d$ (the instance used
here is $d=1$: the projection
$p_2:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\times\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$
and its base changes). Then

$$
Rf_!\bigl({}^pD^{\le0}(X)\bigr)\subset{}^pD^{\le d}(Y),\qquad
Rf_!\bigl({}^pD^{\ge0}(X)\bigr)\subset{}^pD^{\ge -d}(Y).
$$

In the relative-dimension-one instance the $!$-pushforward is exact
for the perverse subcategories up to the shift by one.

external.place: This is Artin–Gabber in the form *the compact-support pushforward along an affine morphism with fibers of dimension at most $d$ has perverse amplitude $\le d$* (Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne, *Faisceaux pervers*, Asterisque 100 (1982), Chapitre 4, § 4.1.2; the proof is the one summarized below).

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C_T=D^b_c(T,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ for $T=X,Y$. Use the actual completed and common-finite-stage operations. The adjunction $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, with both functors preserving these constructible categories, is [lem-per-qbar-ordinary-adjunction]. Relative Verdier duality, biduality and $D_YRf_!\cong Rf_*D_X$ over the same arbitrary field $k$ are [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality]. The middle classes of [def-per-support-condition, def-per-perverse-subcategories] form the bounded t-structure of [lem-per-qbar-middle-tstructure]. Thus $D_T$ interchanges ${}^pD^{\le n}$ and ${}^pD^{\ge -n}$: one implication is the definition of cosupport and the converse follows by biduality. No algebraic-closedness or finite-field assumption is imposed on $k$. The Verdier dual in the cosupport condition of [def-per-support-condition] is there the finite-field dual of the Six-Functors chapter, defined only over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and at finite coefficients $A_{E,n}$; on $\mathcal C_T$ over the field $k$ of the statement the cosupport condition is read with $D_T$ of [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality], exactly as [lem-per-qbar-middle-tstructure] defines ${}^pD^{\ge n}(T)$. This reading of the imported definition is recorded for the maintainer.

source.place: 4.0 and 4.2.4: relative duality and the middle t-structure; modern adic domains specified in the cited helpers

proof.text: Let $A\in{}^pD^{\le0}(Y)$. For each integer $i$ put $F=\mathcal H^{-i}A$, and let $Z$ be the reduced closed support of $F$. By [def-per-support-condition], $\dim Z\le i$. If $i<0$, or $Z$ is empty, then $F=0$. Otherwise [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] gives $\mathcal H^{-i}(Lf^*A)\cong f^*F$ and its fibre formula shows that its support is contained in the closed inverse image $X\times_Y Z$. Its fibres over $Z$ have dimension at most $d$: they are fibres of $f$ followed by residue-field extension, and [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] identifies their local dimensions with the original ones. Apply the second inequality of [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds] to $X\times_Y Z\to Z$ to obtain $\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}(Lf^*A)\le i+d$. This is $Lf^*A\in{}^pD^{\le d}(X)$ by [def-per-perverse-subcategories]. Since pullback commutes with shifts, $Lf^*({}^pD^{\le n}(Y))\subset{}^pD^{\le n+d}(X)$ for all $n$. This is BBD's $Lf^*[d]$ support bound, without a smoothness assumption.

source.place: 4.2.4: the dimension estimate for pullback, expressed using closed supports

proof.text: Let $B\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)$ and $A\in{}^pD^{\le-d-1}(Y)$. Step 2 gives $Lf^*A\in{}^pD^{\le-1}(X)$. Orthogonality in [lem-per-qbar-middle-tstructure] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Lf^*A,B)=0$. By [lem-per-qbar-ordinary-adjunction], $\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*B)=0$. As this holds for every such $A$, the orthogonal characterization in [lem-per-qbar-middle-tstructure] gives $Rf_*B\in{}^pD^{\ge-d}(Y)$. This writes out the adjunction argument of BBD 1.3.17(iii).

source.place: 1.3.17(iii) and 4.2.4: adjunction transfers the pullback support bound

proof.text: Let $K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X)$. By Step 1, $D_XK\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)$, so Step 3 gives $Rf_*D_XK\in{}^pD^{\ge-d}(Y)$. The isomorphism $D_YRf_!K\cong Rf_*D_XK$ of [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality] identifies its left side with this object. Apply $D_Y$, use biduality, and use the interchange of shifted classes from Step 1 to obtain $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\le d}(Y)$. This proves the upper inclusion. No boundary term or induction is needed.

source.place: 4.2.4: the diagonal duality implication from the ordinary direct-image lower bound

proof.text: Now use that $f$ is affine. If $K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X)$, let $F_i=\mathcal H^{-i}K$. Its closed support has dimension at most $i$ by [def-per-support-condition]; a nonzero $F_i$ has $i\ge0$. For $q\ge0$, [lem-per-qbar-affine-support-bound] gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^q(Rf_*F_i)\le i-q$, and it gives zero in negative degrees. The object $Rf_*F_i[i]$ has degree $j=q-i$, so this inequality is exactly $\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^j(Rf_*F_i[i])\le-j$. Thus $Rf_*F_i[i]\in{}^pD^{\le0}(Y)$ by [def-per-perverse-subcategories]. The bounded standard t-structure of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] and the truncation triangles of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] build $K$ from the finitely many $F_i[i]$. Apply the exact triangulated functor $Rf_*$ of [lem-per-qbar-ordinary-adjunction] and extension closure in [lem-per-qbar-middle-tstructure]. It follows that $Rf_*K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(Y)$, the full affine Artin bound.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.1: the sheaf support estimate and bounded ordinary truncations

proof.text: For $K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)$, Step 1 gives $D_XK\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X)$. Step 5 and [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality] yield $D_YRf_!K\cong Rf_*D_XK\in{}^pD^{\le0}(Y)$. By [def-per-support-condition, def-per-perverse-subcategories], this says $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(Y)$. Since $d\ge0$, this class is contained in ${}^pD^{\ge-d}(Y)$ by the shifted t-structure of [lem-per-qbar-middle-tstructure]. This proves the requested lower inclusion, with the stronger affine bound of BBD 4.1.2. If $X$ is empty both inclusions hold for the zero object. The bounds specialize to $d=0$ and $d=1$; applying them to the projection of two affine lines and its stated base changes gives the claimed relative-dimension-one instance.

proof_origin.place: 4.2.4 and 1.3.17(iii) for the upper bound; 4.1.1--4.1.2 for the lower bound, using modern adic categories over arbitrary fields
